evidence.quote: “You will neither torture me nor kill me.”
was glad they could not hear the persistent beating of his heart which gave the lie to his words.

adjudications.reason: The plan explicitly allows condensing paras 58–63, and the 'mind reader' aside was to be kept only 'if space allows'. The draft is over budget. The passage still reads: Tommy's fear at being seen through is followed by outward confidence. The beating heart 'gave the lie to his words', meaning 'You will neither torture me nor kill me'. 'And why am I so confident?' follows naturally from his confident look. Both layers survive, outward flippancy and inner fear. This is a legitimate tradeoff.

evidence.quote: “He gave the word. How was I to know?”
“Dead men tell no tales,” said the German evenly.

adjudications.reason: Tommy was caught listening at the door, and the German has just learned how he got in. 'Dead men tell no tales' therefore coheres as a dismissal: it no longer matters what the spy saw or heard, because he will die. Tommy's 'not dead yet' answers it directly. The plan did not require para 26, and restoring it would cost about 20 words in an over-budget chapter.

evidence.quote: There may be things that you know which I do not.
There may be things that you know which I do not. But equally I’ve got something up my sleeve
“I wonder whether, after all, you know as much as we think?” the German said softly.

adjudications.reason: The German has just asked 'I wonder whether, after all, you know as much as we think?'. Tommy's recovery in the source works by conceding gaps and then countering with 'But equally'. That is the author's qualification, and it is what makes the recovery an essential beat. The first draft kept it, and the revision dropped it, so the reply no longer meets the doubt it answers. Restoring it costs 13 words of source text.

remaining_concerns: The net change is about 26 words removed, against 28 required, so the count will be slightly above target.
The Boris 'you do not' exchange and the 'mind reader' aside remain cut as a budget tradeoff.
